info.title: ki-agent JSON-RPC API
info.description: Control API of the ki-agent, served over JSON-RPC 2.0 on a local Unix socket (newline-delimited JSON) and over WebSocket at /rpc on loopback listeners (direct, and the one the edge routes to). WebSocket clients authenticate with an API token (Authorization: Bearer) or a panel session cookie, and every method requires a role (x-role: viewer, operator or admin). Every connection must start with agent.hello; only agent.hello and rpc.discover may be called before it. Container methods only ever see containers labelled ki.managed=true.

methods.name: rpc.discover
methods.summary: Return this OpenRPC document.
methods.description: May be called before agent.hello.

result.name: document
result.description: The OpenRPC document describing this API.

methods.name: agent.hello
methods.summary: Negotiate the protocol version and open the session.
methods.description: Must be the first call on a connection. The protocol major version must equal the agent's; minor and patch differences are compatible. On a major mismatch the agent answers with an IncompatibleVersion error and then closes the connection. Requests may be pipelined directly behind agent.hello without waiting for its response: they are processed in order and see the completed handshake (requests sent before it succeeds fail with HandshakeRequired).

params.name: protocol
params.description: Protocol semantic version the client speaks.

params.name: client
params.description: Identification of the calling client.

params.name: capabilities
params.description: Optional features the client supports.

methods.name: agent.ping
methods.summary: Check that the agent is responsive.

methods.name: agent.heartbeat.subscribe
methods.summary: Stream periodic agent.heartbeat.update notifications.
methods.description: A snapshot-style stream: if the connection is slow, only the latest heartbeat is delivered. The subscription ends with the connection or on agent.heartbeat.unsubscribe.

params.name: interval_ms
params.description: Requested interval between updates in milliseconds. The agent clamps it to 250..60000. Defaults to 1000.

interval_ms.description: The interval actually applied after clamping.

methods.name: agent.heartbeat.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop a heartbeat subscription.

methods.name: agent.heartbeat.update
methods.summary: Notification sent by the agent for a heartbeat subscription.
methods.description: Sent from agent to client; it has no id and expects no response. It is not a callable method.

params.name: update
params.description: The subscription update envelope; data carries a heartbeat.

methods.name: containers.logs.subscribe
methods.summary: Stream a container's log output as containers.logs.update notifications.
methods.description: An ordered stream (see SubscriptionUpdate): lines are never replaced by newer ones, and a slow consumer sees a gap marker instead. The stream follows the container until containers.logs.unsubscribe, the end of the connection, or the container stopping; in the last case a final update with data {"eof": true} is sent and the subscription is closed. If the log stream fails mid-way the final update also carries an error message. The container is checked before the subscription id is returned, so an unknown container fails the call with NotFound. Subscriptions do not support resuming by sequence number: resubscribe with since.

params.name: id
params.description: Container id (full or unambiguous prefix) or name.

params.name: tail
params.description: Number of most recent lines to send first. Defaults to 100; values above 10000 are clamped to 10000.

params.name: since
params.description: Only lines newer than this RFC 3339 timestamp. Use the time of the last line received (with timestamps enabled) to resume after a reconnect.

params.name: timestamps
params.description: Include the time of each line in the updates. Defaults to false.

methods.name: containers.logs.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop a log subscription.

methods.name: containers.logs.update
methods.summary: Notification sent by the agent for a log subscription.
methods.description: Sent from agent to client; it has no id and expects no response. It is not a callable method.

params.name: update
params.description: The subscription update envelope; data carries a log line or the final end-of-stream marker.

methods.name: projects.create
methods.summary: Register a Git repository, a stored Compose file, or a single image as a project.
methods.description: Pass repo_url for a git project, compose for a compose project or image for an image project (mutually exclusive; one of them is required). A compose project has no repository: the content is validated (compose_invalid or policy_violation, with build sections rejected as build_not_allowed, are reported as InvalidParams data) and stored as version 1, the project is ready at once, no webhook secret is returned and its webhook is not reachable; slug is required. Deploy it with deploys.trigger and change it with projects.compose.set. For a git project, auth is inferred: token given means https_token (the URL must be https); an ssh URL means ssh_key (the agent generates a deploy key); an https URL without a token means none. For none and https_token the repository is probed and cloned before anything is stored: any failure leaves nothing behind. For ssh_key the project is stored as pending_access without cloning and the public key is returned; add it as a read-only deploy key, then call projects.verify. The webhook secret is returned only here and on rotation. An image project is a compose project whose Compose file the agent generates from the image spec (stored as version 1 with the note "generated from image", validated like any version; slug is required); the image must carry a tag or digest, latest is refused. Release a new image with projects.image.set.

params.name: repo_url
params.description: Repository URL: https://host/path, ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path or user@host:path. Immutable. Required unless compose is given.

params.name: slug
params.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters. Defaults to the repository name; required with compose. Immutable.

params.name: branch
params.description: Deploy on pushes to this branch. Mutually exclusive with tag_pattern. With neither, the remote default branch is used.

params.name: tag_pattern
params.description: Deploy on tags whose name matches this glob (Go path.Match syntax). Mutually exclusive with branch.

params.name: compose_file
params.description: Compose file path relative to the repository root; absolute paths, .. and symlinks leaving the checkout are rejected. Defaults to the first of compose.yaml, compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml, docker-compose.yml.

params.name: token
params.description: https access token for a private repository. Stored encrypted; never returned.

params.name: token_user
params.description: Basic-auth user paired with the token. Defaults to x-access-token.

params.name: compose
params.description: Compose file content of a compose project, at most 256 KiB. Only prebuilt images are allowed: no build, include, extends or env_file paths. Mutually exclusive with repo_url and the git-only parameters.

params.name: image
params.description: Image spec of an image project; the agent generates the Compose file. Slug is required. Mutually exclusive with repo_url and compose.

webhook_secret.description: Shared secret for verifying webhook deliveries. Shown only once. Absent for compose projects.

methods.name: projects.get
methods.summary: Return one project.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

methods.name: projects.list
methods.summary: List projects sorted by slug.

methods.name: projects.update
methods.summary: Change a project's trigger, compose file or credentials.
methods.description: Setting branch clears tag_pattern and vice versa. token and token_user apply only to https_token projects; rotate_deploy_key only to ssh_key projects and puts the project back to pending_access. A compose_file is validated against the checkout when one exists. Omitted parameters leave the setting unchanged.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: branch
params.description: Deploy on pushes to this branch.

params.name: tag_pattern
params.description: Deploy on tags matching this glob.

params.name: compose_file
params.description: Compose file path relative to the repository root.

params.name: token
params.description: https access token for a private repository. Stored encrypted; never returned.

params.name: token_user
params.description: Basic-auth user paired with the token. Defaults to x-access-token.

params.name: rotate_webhook_secret
params.description: Generate a new webhook secret and return it.

params.name: rotate_deploy_key
params.description: Generate a new deploy key (ssh_key projects only).

webhook_secret.description: The new webhook secret; present only when rotate_webhook_secret was set. Shown only once.

methods.name: projects.verify
methods.summary: Check repository access and bring the checkout up to date.
methods.description: Git projects only; a compose project is rejected as InvalidParams (not a git project). Probes the repository with the stored credentials, resolves the default branch, clones the checkout if there is none (otherwise fetches and checks out the trigger branch head), and locates the compose file. On success the project becomes ready. On failure the status is unchanged, status_detail records the reason, and RepositoryError is returned.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

methods.name: projects.delete
methods.summary: Remove a project, its containers and its checkout.
methods.description: The project's containers and networks (and volumes when requested) are removed first; if the runtime is unavailable nothing is deleted. Then the checkout and the project record are removed.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: volumes
params.description: Also remove the project's volumes. Defaults to false.

methods.name: projects.compose.get
methods.summary: Return the content of a compose project's stored Compose file.
methods.description: Only for compose projects (source compose); a git project is rejected as InvalidParams (not a compose project).

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: version
params.description: Version number. 0 or absent: the latest.

methods.name: projects.compose.set
methods.summary: Store a new version of a compose project's Compose file, optionally deploying it.
methods.description: The content is validated like projects.create (compose_invalid or policy_violation, including build_not_allowed, are reported as InvalidParams data) and stored as the next version number; nothing is stored on rejection. With deploy true a deploy of the new version is queued (as with deploys.trigger, ref compose@v<N>) and returned; if queuing fails the version stays stored and the error is returned. Rolling back is deploys.rollback.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: compose
params.description: Compose file content, at most 256 KiB.

params.name: note
params.description: Free-text note kept with the version.

params.name: deploy
params.description: Queue a deploy of the new version. Default false.

deploy.description: The queued deploy; present only when deploy was true.

methods.name: projects.image.set
methods.summary: Change the image of one service of a compose project and store the result as a new version, optionally deploying it.
methods.description: Works on any compose project. Give exactly one of image (a full new reference) or tag (replaces the tag or digest of the service's current reference). The pinning rule applies: a tag or digest is required and latest is refused. The rest of the Compose file is kept; the result is validated like projects.compose.set and stored as the next version (nothing is stored on rejection). service defaults to the only service that has an image; if several do, the call fails with InvalidParams listing them. With deploy true a deploy of the new version is queued and returned; if queuing fails the version stays stored and the error is returned.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: image
params.description: Full new image reference, with tag or digest. Mutually exclusive with tag.

params.name: tag
params.description: New tag or digest (for example 1.2.4 or sha256:...) for the service's current reference. Mutually exclusive with image.

params.name: service
params.description: Service to change. Defaults to the only service with an image.

params.name: note
params.description: Free-text note kept with the version. Defaults to the new image reference.

params.name: deploy
params.description: Queue a deploy of the new version. Default false.

image.description: The image reference now set on the service.

deploy.description: The queued deploy; present only when deploy was true.

methods.name: projects.compose.history
methods.summary: List the stored versions of a compose project's Compose file, newest first.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: limit
params.description: Return at most this many versions. 0 or absent: all.

deployed.description: True when a succeeded deploy ran this version.

methods.name: projects.env.set
methods.summary: Set project environment variables.
methods.description: Merges vars into the project's stored variables; existing names are overwritten, others are kept. Values are encrypted at rest and never returned by any method. At deploy time they are written to the checkout's .env file and also used for ${VAR} interpolation of the compose file. Names must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$; a project holds at most 256 variables, values are at most 64 KiB and must not contain NUL.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: vars
params.description: Variables to set, name to value.

methods.name: projects.env.unset
methods.summary: Remove project environment variables.
methods.description: Removes the named variables; names that are not set are ignored.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: names
params.description: Variable names to remove.

methods.name: projects.env.list
methods.summary: List the names of a project's environment variables.
methods.description: Never returns values.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

methods.name: projects.expose
methods.summary: Publish a service of a project on one or more domains through the edge proxy.
methods.description: Stores a project-side exposure for the service, which overrides any ki.expose.* labels of that service entirely. A domain is routed to at most one (project, service) on the server: if another project already exposes one of the domains the call fails with AlreadyExists and data {domain, project}. The server's own hostnames (edge.domain and hostnames with an installed certificate) are reserved and rejected with InvalidParams. The service is not required to exist yet; projects.get reports a warning in exposure_warnings while it is unverified. Returns the updated project.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: service
params.description: Compose service name.

params.name: port
params.description: Container port the service listens on.

params.name: domains
params.description: Lowercase DNS names (ASCII or punycode, at least one dot, no wildcards, not IP addresses), 1 to 20.

params.name: path
params.description: Optional path prefix; must start with /, at most 256 characters, no spaces or '..'.

methods.name: projects.unexpose
methods.summary: Remove the project-side exposure of a service.
methods.description: Deletes the project-side entry for the service; the ki.expose.* labels of the last successful deploy, if any, apply again. Removing a service without a project-side entry is a no-op. Returns the updated project.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: service
params.description: Compose service name.

methods.name: projects.services
methods.summary: List the services of a project with their containers and health.
methods.description: Built from the last deployed model plus any running container labelled with a service that is not in it. A service in the model without a container has state missing. Exposure is the effective exposure entry of the service, when there is one.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

methods.name: projects.services.start
methods.summary: Start every container of a service.
methods.description: Starts every container of the service. Returns the updated service. A service that is neither in the deployed model nor backed by a container fails with NotFound. Not serialised against a running deploy.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: service
params.description: Compose service name.

methods.name: projects.services.stop
methods.summary: Stop every container of a service.
methods.description: Stops every container of the service, with a 10 second grace period. Returns the updated service. A service that is neither in the deployed model nor backed by a container fails with NotFound. Not serialised against a running deploy.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: service
params.description: Compose service name.

methods.name: projects.services.restart
methods.summary: Restart every container of a service.
methods.description: Restarts every container of the service, with a 10 second grace period. Returns the updated service. A service that is neither in the deployed model nor backed by a container fails with NotFound. Not serialised against a running deploy.

params.name: slug
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: service
params.description: Compose service name.

methods.name: deploys.trigger
methods.summary: Queue a deploy of a project.
methods.description: Checks that the project is ready and that ref is allowed for the project's trigger, records a queued deploy and returns it (status running when it started at once). One deploy runs per project at a time; at most one waits behind it, and a newer trigger supersedes the waiting one. A running deploy is never cancelled by a trigger. Pipeline failures are not errors of this call: they are recorded on the deploy (status failed, error). The source is api, or cli when called over the Unix socket.

params.name: project
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: ref
params.description: What to deploy: refs/heads/<branch>, refs/tags/<tag>, a bare branch or tag name, or a full 40 or 64 hex digit commit sha. Absent: the head of the trigger branch, or the newest tag matching the trigger's tag_pattern. Only refs matching the project's trigger are allowed (the trigger branch, or tags matching the pattern; a sha must be reachable from the branch head or be pointed at by a matching tag). For a compose project the ref is a stored version: compose@v<N>, v<N> or <N>; absent means the latest version.

methods.name: deploys.rollback
methods.summary: Re-deploy an earlier successful deploy.
methods.description: Queues a normal deploy (the whole pipeline runs again) of the target deploy's ref pinned to the target's commit; the new deploy has rollback_of set to the target. The target is the given deploy, which must belong to the project, have succeeded and have a commit; when deploy is absent it is the newest succeeded deploy older than the newest succeeded one (the previous good deploy). With no such deploy the call fails with DeployError reason no_rollback_target. A commit that is no longer reachable from its ref (force-pushed branch) fails at the fetch stage of the new deploy. Queueing rules are those of deploys.trigger. The source is api, or cli over the Unix socket.

params.name: project
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: deploy
params.description: Deploy id to return to. Defaults to the previous good deploy.

methods.name: deploys.get
methods.summary: Get a deploy.

params.name: id
params.description: Deploy id.

methods.name: deploys.list
methods.summary: List a project's deploys, newest first.
methods.description: History is kept per project up to deploys.keep entries (default 50).

params.name: project
params.description: Project slug.

params.name: limit
params.description: Defaults to 20; values above 100 are clamped to 100.

params.name: before_id
params.description: Only deploys with a smaller id; pass the last id of the previous page to paginate.

methods.name: deploys.subscribe
methods.summary: Stream a deploy's log and final status as deploys.update notifications.
methods.description: An ordered stream (see SubscriptionUpdate). The stored log is replayed first (lines after since_seq), then live lines follow; the stream ends with a status update carrying the final Deploy, after which the subscription is closed by the agent. Subscribing to a finished deploy replays its stored log and then sends the final status. The deploy is checked before the subscription id is returned, so an unknown deploy fails with NotFound.

params.name: id
params.description: Deploy id.

params.name: since_seq
params.description: Replay only stored log lines with a seq greater than this; use the seq of the last line received to resume after a reconnect. Defaults to 0 (everything).

methods.name: deploys.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop a deploy subscription.

methods.name: deploys.update
methods.summary: Notification sent by the agent for a deploy subscription.
methods.description: Sent from agent to client; it has no id and expects no response. It is not a callable method.

params.name: update
params.description: The subscription update envelope; data carries a log line or the final status.

methods.name: host.stats
methods.summary: Read the latest host resource sample and optionally its recent history.
methods.description: Never blocks on sampling: current is null until the agent has taken its first sample (shortly after start). The agent samples every monitor.host_interval, faster while host.subscribe subscriptions exist; history holds one sample per monitor.history_resolution slot for up to monitor.history. With per_core true the call may wait up to 2 seconds for a sample that carries the per-core breakdown. Rates (cpu.percent and every *_per_s field) are null in the first sample after the agent starts. Inside a container the figures describe the container's view of the host unless the host's /proc and /sys are mounted (see the README).

params.name: history
params.description: Include the retained samples, oldest first. Defaults to false.

params.name: per_core
params.description: Include cpu.per_core. Defaults to false.

history.description: Present only when history was requested.

methods.name: host.subscribe
methods.summary: Receive host resource samples as host.update notifications.
methods.description: A snapshot stream (see SubscriptionUpdate): a slow consumer sees the latest sample. The first update is sent as soon as a sample exists. While subscriptions exist the agent samples at the fastest requested interval (never slower than monitor.host_interval); it returns to the configured interval when the last one ends.

params.name: interval_ms
params.description: Requested interval between updates in milliseconds. The agent clamps it to 1000..60000. Defaults to 2000.

params.name: per_core
params.description: Include cpu.per_core in the samples. Defaults to false.

interval_ms.description: The interval actually applied after clamping.

methods.name: host.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop a host.subscribe subscription.

methods.name: host.update
methods.summary: Notification sent by the agent for a host.subscribe subscription.
methods.description: Sent from agent to client; it has no id and expects no response. It is not a callable method.

params.name: update
params.description: The subscription update envelope; data is {sample: HostSample}.

methods.name: containers.stats
methods.summary: Read the latest resource sample of the managed containers.
methods.description: Covers the running containers ki manages plus the edge proxy. Never blocks on sampling: a container's current is null until its first sample exists. The agent samples every monitor.container_interval, faster while containers.stats.subscribe subscriptions exist. available is false (and containers empty) when the container engine cannot be reached; this is not an error. A container that appeared since the previous sample has null rates (cpu_percent, *_per_s) in its first sample. An unmanaged or unknown id fails with NotFound.

params.name: project
params.description: Only containers of this project slug.

params.name: id
params.description: Only this container: the full id or a prefix of at least 12 characters.

params.name: history
params.description: Include the retained samples of each container, oldest first. Defaults to false.

history.description: Present only when history was requested.

methods.name: containers.stats.subscribe
methods.summary: Receive container resource samples as containers.stats.update notifications.
methods.description: A snapshot stream (see SubscriptionUpdate). Each update carries the latest sample of every selected container; the first is sent once a sampling round has completed. While subscriptions exist the agent samples at the fastest requested interval (never slower than monitor.container_interval). An unmanaged id fails with NotFound; an unreachable engine fails with RuntimeUnavailable.

params.name: project
params.description: Only containers of this project slug.

params.name: id
params.description: Only this container: the full id or a prefix of at least 12 characters.

params.name: interval_ms
params.description: Requested interval between updates in milliseconds. The agent clamps it to 2000..60000. Defaults to 5000.

interval_ms.description: The interval actually applied after clamping.

methods.name: containers.stats.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop a containers.stats.subscribe subscription.

methods.name: containers.stats.update
methods.summary: Notification sent by the agent for a containers.stats.subscribe subscription.
methods.description: Sent from agent to client; it has no id and expects no response. It is not a callable method.

params.name: update
params.description: The subscription update envelope; data is {available, containers: ContainerSample[]}.

methods.name: aws.status
methods.summary: Report whether the server is an EC2 instance and which AWS agents run on it.
methods.description: Uses IMDSv2 only (never reads instance credentials); answers from a 10 minute cache and, off EC2, within about a second. The AWS agents are detected without root from systemd unit state; their registration is not visible locally. Capability aws.

methods.name: tunnel.status
methods.summary: Report the state of the managed Cloudflare Tunnel.
methods.description: Always available (capability tunnel): with the tunnel disabled the result has enabled false and state disabled. ready comes from the connector's own readiness endpoint, connections is the number of active connections to Cloudflare. warnings lists configuration problems such as an edge that is not in behind mode. The result never contains the token.

methods.name: tunnel.configure
methods.summary: Store the Cloudflare Tunnel token and (re)start the connector (local socket and control plane only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted: other transports are refused with Unauthorized. The token (the base64 string Cloudflare shows for a remotely managed tunnel) is stored in a 0600 file under the data directory and handed to the connector as a mounted token file; it is never echoed, logged or returned. The connector only runs when tunnel.enabled is true. Replacing the token restarts the connector. Returns the updated tunnel status.

params.name: token
params.description: Tunnel token: 1 to 4096 characters of base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / = - _).

methods.name: tunnel.remove
methods.summary: Delete the stored tunnel token and remove the connector (local socket and control plane only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted like tunnel.configure. Deletes the token, stops and removes the connector container. Idempotent. Returns the updated tunnel status.

methods.name: edge.status
methods.summary: Report the state of the edge proxy.
methods.description: Always available: with the edge disabled the result has enabled false and state disabled. The self-signed fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the default certificate served for the bare IP and unknown hosts; operators compare it when they accept that certificate by hand.

methods.name: edge.csr
methods.summary: Create a certificate signing request for a server hostname (local socket and control plane only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted: other transports are refused with Unauthorized. Generates (or reuses the pending) ECDSA P-256 key for the hostname, kept on the server and never returned, and returns a PEM CSR with that single DNS name. The control plane has it signed (for example by an origin CA) and passes the certificate to edge.certificate.install. A hostname exposed by a project is refused with AlreadyExists.

params.name: hostname
params.description: Server hostname (lowercase DNS name).

methods.name: edge.certificate.install
methods.summary: Install the certificate for a server hostname (local socket and control plane only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted like edge.csr. The leaf must match the key created by edge.csr, cover the hostname, be valid now and not expire within 24 hours; violations are InvalidParams with a message. The chain is not verified against system roots: an origin CA certificate trusted only by a CDN is accepted. After the install the hostname becomes a server hostname served with this certificate and cannot be exposed by projects. Returns the updated edge status.

params.name: hostname
params.description: Server hostname the certificate is for.

params.name: certificate
params.description: PEM certificate chain, leaf first.

methods.name: edge.certificate.import
methods.summary: Import a bring-your-own certificate and key (local socket only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted to the Unix socket: the private key is never accepted from the control plane or the HTTP API. The key must match the leaf, the leaf must be valid now and not expire within 24 hours; the names are the leaf's DNS subject alternative names, wildcards (*.example.com, one label deep) allowed. The certificate is stored under the data directory and keyed by a stable id derived from its names; importing the same names again replaces it. A project router whose every domain is covered by an installed or imported certificate is served with it instead of ACME. With server true the non-wildcard names become server hostnames (panel, hooks) and are subject to the reserved-hostname rule. Returns the updated edge status.

params.name: certificate
params.description: PEM certificate chain, leaf first.

params.name: key
params.description: PEM private key matching the leaf.

params.name: server
params.description: Mark the non-wildcard names as server hostnames. Default false.

methods.name: edge.certificate.remove
methods.summary: Remove an installed or imported certificate and key (local socket and control plane only).
methods.description: Transport-restricted like edge.csr. Pass id (an imported certificate's id from edge.status) or hostname (a server hostname with an installed certificate); id wins when both are given. Deletes the certificate and key. Returns the updated edge status.

params.name: id
params.description: Certificate id as reported by edge.status.

params.name: hostname
params.description: Server hostname with an installed certificate.

methods.name: enrollment.start
methods.summary: Start enrolling the agent with a control plane (local socket only).
methods.description: Local-only: any transport other than the Unix socket is refused with Unauthorized. Discovers the enrollment endpoints under url, requests a device code and returns the code the operator must approve. Polling then runs in the background, bound to this connection: it is cancelled when the connection closes. Call enrollment.wait on the same connection to learn the outcome. On approval the credentials are stored in the data directory and the outbound control-plane connection starts at once, replacing any configured one. Only one enrollment may be in progress per agent.

params.name: url
params.description: Enrollment base URL (https; http only for loopback hosts). Defaults to the URL built into the binary; without either the call fails with InvalidParams.

params.name: force
params.description: Enroll again even if credentials exist. Defaults to false.

methods.name: enrollment.wait
methods.summary: Wait for the enrollment started on this connection to finish (local socket only).
methods.description: Local-only. Blocks until the operator approves the code and the credentials are stored, then returns the control plane URL. Fails with EnrollmentError (reason denied, expired, unreachable, invalid_response or failed) if the enrollment does not succeed, and with InvalidParams if this connection has no enrollment in progress.

control_plane_url.description: WebSocket endpoint the agent now connects to.

methods.name: enrollment.remove
methods.summary: Forget the enrollment and stop its connection (local socket only).
methods.description: Local-only. Deletes the stored credentials and stops the enrolled control-plane connection, cancelling any enrollment in progress. If the config file defines a control plane, the agent connects to that one instead. Fails with NotFound ("not enrolled") when there are no stored credentials.

methods.name: auth.whoami
methods.summary: Return the identity the connection is authenticated as.
methods.description: Works for every principal: panel users and API tokens report their name and role, the local Unix socket reports kind local (admin) and the control-plane connection kind control-plane (admin).

methods.name: users.list
methods.summary: List panel users.
methods.description: Returns every user, newest last. Password hashes and TOTP secrets are never returned.

methods.name: users.create
methods.summary: Create a user and issue a one-time setup link.
methods.description: The user starts in status pending and cannot sign in until the person opens the setup link, chooses a password and enrols an authenticator app. The link is valid for 30 minutes and works once; it is returned only here, so hand it over right away. Issuing a new link for the user invalidates older ones.

params.name: username
params.description: Lowercase letters, digits, '_', '.', '-'; 2 to 32 characters, starting with a letter.

params.name: role
params.description: Role of the new user.

methods.name: users.update
methods.summary: Change a user's role or disable or enable the account.
methods.description: Changing the role or disabling the account ends the user's sessions and closes its open connections. The last active admin cannot be disabled or demoted (InvalidParams). Enabling restores the status the user had (active or pending).

params.name: username
params.description: User to change.

params.name: role
params.description: New role.

params.name: disabled
params.description: true disables the account, false enables it.

methods.name: users.reset
methods.summary: Reset a user's password and authenticator and issue a new setup link.
methods.description: Clears the password and TOTP secret, ends the user's sessions, closes its open connections and sets the status to pending. Use it for lost devices and forgotten passwords.

params.name: username
params.description: User to reset.

methods.name: users.delete
methods.summary: Delete a user.
methods.description: Ends the user's sessions and closes its open connections. The last active admin cannot be deleted (InvalidParams).

params.name: username
params.description: User to delete.

methods.name: panel.setup
methods.summary: Create the first panel admin and return the setup link.
methods.description: Only works while no active admin exists: it creates (or reuses the pending) admin and issues a setup link. When an active admin exists the call fails with InvalidParams; use users.reset instead. The link host is panel.public_url, else edge.domain, else an installed control-plane hostname, else the host's first non-loopback IPv4 address; with the edge disabled it is the direct listener, http://127.0.0.1:8091 by default (with an IP address, fingerprint_sha256 carries the fingerprint of the edge's self-signed certificate to compare in the browser).

params.name: username
params.description: Name of the admin. Defaults to "admin".

methods.name: tokens.create
methods.summary: Create an API token.
methods.description: The secret is returned only in this response and cannot be retrieved later. Tokens authenticate WebSocket connections with an Authorization: Bearer header on the direct listener (and on the edge only when api.public_tokens is true).

params.name: name
params.description: Unique name, letters, digits, '_', '.', '-'.

params.name: role
params.description: Role the token acts with.

params.name: expires_in
params.description: Lifetime as a Go duration (for example 720h); at most one year. Omitted: the token does not expire.

methods.name: tokens.list
methods.summary: List API tokens.
methods.description: Never includes the secrets. Revoked tokens remain listed with revoked true.

methods.name: tokens.revoke
methods.summary: Revoke an API token.
methods.description: The token stops working at once and connections opened with it are closed.

params.name: name
params.description: Token name.

methods.name: audit.list
methods.summary: List the audit log, newest first.
methods.description: Records every call to an operator or admin method (success or error) and the authentication events login, login failure, setup, logout and lockout. Denied calls are not recorded. Targets are slugs, names or ids, never secrets or values. The log keeps the newest 10000 entries. Page with before_id set to the smallest id received.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum entries, 1 to 500. Defaults to 100.

params.name: before_id
params.description: Return only entries with a smaller id.

HostSample.description: One host measurement. time is when the agent took the sample. Rate fields (cpu.percent and every *_per_s) are null in the first sample after the agent starts and whenever a counter went backwards; they are computed from consecutive samples.

disks.description: The filesystems holding / and data_dir plus monitor.disk_paths, de-duplicated by device.

disk_io.description: Summed over whole block devices (partitions, loop and ram devices are not counted).

network.description: Summed over the interfaces other than lo, veth*, docker*, br-*, cni*, flannel* and virbr*.

ContainerSample.description: One container measurement. time is when the agent took the sample. Rate fields (cpu_percent and every *_per_s) are null in a container's first sample and right after it restarted.

project.description: Project slug; empty for containers outside a project.

service.description: Compose service name; empty outside a project.

component.description: Empty for project services; the edge proxy reports its component name.

cpu_percent.description: Percent of one core: 100 is one fully used core and the value can exceed 100 with several cores.

usage.description: Bytes, without reclaimable file cache (like docker stats).

percent.description: Null when there is no limit.

SubscriptionID.description: Opaque subscription identifier (128 random bits, hex encoded).

ControlPlaneStatus.description: State of the agent's outbound connection to a control plane.

source.description: Where the active settings came from; absent while disabled. Stored enrollment credentials take precedence over the config file.

url.description: Control plane endpoint without userinfo, query or fragment.

last_error.description: Why the most recent connection attempt failed or the connection ended.

reconnects.description: Connection attempts made after the first one.

EnrollmentAuthorization.description: A pending device-flow authorization the operator must approve.

user_code.description: Short code to enter or confirm at the verification page.

verification_uri.description: Page where the operator enters the code.

verification_uri_complete.description: Same page with the code filled in; present when the control plane provides it.

expires_at.description: When the code stops being valid.

Gap.description: Inclusive range of sequence numbers that were dropped before delivery.

SubscriptionUpdate.description: Params of every <namespace>.update notification. Exactly one of data and gap is present. seq increases monotonically per subscription starting at 1; a snapshot stream may skip values. When gap is present (ordered streams that overflowed) seq equals gap.to, so the sequence stays contiguous with the next update.

data.description: The update payload, defined per subscription method.

health.description: Absent when the container has no health check.

time.description: Present only when the subscription asked for timestamps.

text.description: The line without its newline. Lines over 64 KiB are truncated and end in a truncation marker.

LogEnd.description: Final update of a log subscription: the container stopped and the stream ended.

error.description: Present when the stream ended because of a failure rather than the container stopping.

ImageSpec.description: Inputs of an image project; the agent generates a single-service Compose file from them.

image.description: Full image reference with registry, for example registry.example.com/team/app:1.2.3, ghcr.io/acme/web@sha256:... or nginx:1.27. A tag or digest is required; latest is refused.

port.description: Container port to publish through the edge.

domains.description: Domains routed to the port; requires port.

volumes.description: Named volumes as name:/container/path[:ro]; bind mounts are refused.

env.description: Plain, non-secret variables written to the Compose file. Secrets go through projects.env.set.

ComposeVersion.description: One stored version of a compose project's Compose file.

rule.description: Stable rule identifier, for example privileged.

ProjectTrigger.description: What a push must match to deploy. Exactly one member is set once known; both are absent for an ssh_key project created without a branch until projects.verify resolves the default branch.

tag_pattern.description: Glob matched against the tag name.

ProjectAuth.description: How the agent authenticates to the repository. Private keys and tokens are never returned.

public_key.description: Deploy key to authorise on the repository (ssh_key only).

token_user.description: Basic-auth user paired with the token (https_token only).

source.description: git: deployed from a repository. compose: deployed from a stored Compose file of prebuilt images; repo_url, trigger, default_branch, compose_file, auth, webhook and commit are then empty.

compose_version.description: Latest stored compose version; present only for compose projects.

default_branch.description: Remote HEAD branch; empty until known.

compose_file.description: Path relative to the checkout; empty until known.

path.description: HTTP path of the project's webhook endpoint, /hooks/<id>.

status_detail.description: Last access or clone failure, human readable.

commit.description: Checked-out commit sha; empty when there is no checkout.

exposure.description: Effective exposure: project-side entries plus label entries of services without a project-side entry. Absent when nothing is exposed.

exposure_warnings.description: Advisory notes about the exposure, for example a service that is not in the deployed model or a label domain that another project owns (so it is not routed). Absent when there are none.

Exposure.description: A service published through the edge proxy.

path.description: Optional path prefix; absent when the whole host is routed.

source.description: labels: ki.expose.* labels of the last successful deploy; project: set with projects.expose, overrides the labels.
How the agent is installed; empty when not installed.

detected.description: False when the metadata service is unreachable (not on EC2); the other fields are then absent.

instance_profile_arn.description: Absent when the instance has no role.

imds_v1_enabled.description: True when an unauthenticated (IMDSv1) request succeeds; recommended to disable.

state.description: unconfigured: enabled but no token stored. starting: the connector was just (re)started. disconnected: running without an active connection to Cloudflare.

ready.description: The connector reports an active connection to Cloudflare.

last_error.description: Why the edge is in state error (for example a port in use or a failed image pull); the agent keeps retrying. Absent otherwise.

mode.description: front: the edge owns the public ports. behind: it listens on loopback plain HTTP behind another web server that owns TLS.

listen.description: Address the proxy binds in behind mode (edge.behind_listen); absent in front mode.

server_hostnames.description: Hostnames the server itself answers on (edge.domain and hostnames with an installed certificate). Projects cannot expose these.

self_signed.description: The persistent self-signed default certificate served for the bare IP and unknown hosts.

fingerprint_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the certificate (DER) as colon-separated uppercase hex pairs.

id.description: Pass to edge.certificate.remove: the hostname for acme and installed certificates, i-<hex> for imported ones.

names.description: DNS names covered; imported certificates may hold wildcards.

server.description: True when the certificate serves server hostnames.

not_after.description: Known for installed and imported certificates.

routes.description: Number of project routes currently served.

PruneReport.description: Counts of resources removed for a project.

kept_volumes.description: Names of anonymous volumes of the removed containers that were kept because volumes were not requested. They carry no project label, so they can no longer be found through the project and may hold data; remove them with docker volume rm. Empty when volumes were removed or there were none.

EnvNames.description: Names of all variables of a project after the change.

ref.description: The requested ref, normalized (refs/heads/..., refs/tags/... or a sha; compose@v<N> for a compose project).

commit.description: Resolved commit sha; empty until the checkout stage has run, and always empty for compose projects.

status.description: superseded: replaced in the queue by a newer trigger. interrupted: cancelled by agent shutdown or project deletion, or left unfinished by a previous agent process.

stage.description: Last pipeline stage reached; empty while queued. prepare (compose projects) writes the stored version into the project directory in place of fetch.

rollback_of.description: Id of the deploy this one re-deploys; present only on rollbacks.

DeployFailure.description: Why a deploy failed; present only when status is failed.

rule.description: Stable rule identifier, for example privileged.

health.description: Health check status (healthy, unhealthy, starting) or empty when the container has no health check.

started_at.description: Absent when the container has never started.

image.description: Image from the deployed model, else from a running container; absent when unknown.

state.description: missing: in the deployed model but without a container. unhealthy: any container is unhealthy or restarting. partial: some, not all, containers are running.

seq.description: Stored line number, usable as since_seq. Absent for lines beyond the per-deploy log cap (deploys.log_max_bytes), which are streamed live but not stored.

stream.description: agent lines are the agent's own stage markers.

Role.description: viewer < operator < admin; each role includes the ones below it. See the x-role of every method.

setup_url.description: One-time link; the token is in the URL fragment so it never reaches server logs.

fingerprint_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the edge's self-signed certificate; present only when the link host is an IP address.

InvalidParams.data: For a rejected Compose file (projects.create, projects.compose.set): object {reason, detail, violations?}; reason is compose_invalid or policy_violation, and violations ([{service, rule, detail}], see the PolicyViolations schema) is present for policy_violation, for example rule build_not_allowed.

Unauthorized.data: -32001 is returned for local-only methods (enrollment.*) over any transport other than the Unix socket, and as "forbidden: requires <role>" when the caller's role is below the method's x-role.

NotFound.data: Also returned for containers that exist but are not managed by ki. The projects.* methods return it with the message "project not found".

PolicyViolation.data: Object {violations: [{service, rule, detail}]}; see the PolicyViolations schema.

AlreadyExists.data: Only for domain conflicts (projects.expose, edge.csr, edge.certificate.install): object {domain, project} (edge methods add service) naming the domain and the project that exposes it; absent for a duplicate project.

RepositoryError.data: Object {reason, detail}; reason is one of invalid_url, unreachable, auth_failed, not_found, ref_not_found, compose_not_found, failed.

EnrollmentError.data: Object {reason, detail}; reason is one of unreachable, invalid_response, denied, expired, failed.

DeployError.data: Object {reason, detail}; reason is one of project_not_ready, ref_not_allowed, ref_not_found, no_rollback_target; see the DeployError schema.
